source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 2: book page 176 (PDF 181); its answer is key entry 3 on PDF 307 (x = 2 lies on the curve), not entry 2; checked with sympy and the solution book (PDF 860-861).

blocks.prompt: 2. A dataset is modeled by the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 5x - 2\). Find whether the point \(x = 2\) lies on the curve.
blocks.explanation:
This is the Factor Theorem in words: the point \(x = 2\) "lies on the curve" here means the model is zero there, \(P(2) = 0\) (the curve meets the \(x\)-axis at \(x = 2\)).
We must decide yes or no.
Plan: work out \(P(2)\); if it is 0, the answer is yes and \(x - 2\) is a factor; check by division.
steps:
Given: \(P(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 5x - 2\), the point \(x = 2\).
To find: whether \(x = 2\) lies on the curve, i.e. whether \(P(2) = 0\).
Method: Factor Theorem: \(x - 2\) is a factor of \(P(x)\) exactly when \(P(2) = 0\). So we only need the value \(P(2)\).

Work out \(P(2)\)
\[P(2) = 2^3 - 4(2)^2 + 5(2) - 2\]
\[= 8 - 4(4) + 10 - 2\]
\[= 8 - 16 + 10 - 2\]
\[= 0\]
Why: Substituting \(x = 2\) gives the remainder on division by \(x - 2\) (Remainder Theorem). Powers first, then multiply, then add from left to right: \(8 - 16 = -8\), \(-8 + 10 = 2\), \(2 - 2 = 0\).

Draw the conclusion
\[P(2) = 0\]
\[\Rightarrow (x - 2) \text{ is a factor}\]
Why: A zero value means zero remainder, so by the Factor Theorem \(x - 2\) divides \(P(x)\) exactly and \(x = 2\) is a root: the point \(x = 2\) lies on the curve (on the \(x\)-axis).

Check by synthetic division by \(x - 2\)
Coefficients \(1,\ -4,\ 5,\ -2\) with \(a = 2\):
bring down 1; \(1 \times 2 = 2\), \(-4 + 2 = -2\);
\(-2 \times 2 = -4\), \(5 - 4 = 1\);
\(1 \times 2 = 2\), \(-2 + 2 = 0\).
\[\text{Quotient} = x^2 - 2x + 1\]
\[\text{Remainder} = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[P(x) = (x - 2)(x - 1)^2\]
Why: Synthetic division (Section 9.1.3) gives the same remainder 0, and the quotient \(x^2 - 2x + 1 = (x - 1)^2\) even shows the full factorization.
blocks.final_answer: Yes. \(P(2) = 0\), so \(x = 2\) lies on the curve (and \(x - 2\) is a factor: \(P(x) = (x - 2)(x - 1)^2\)).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the answer key (PDF 307) the answer to this question is printed as entry 3, "\(x = 2\) lies on the curve", which agrees with our working. Entry 2 ("\(x = -1\) is a valid point") does not belong to this question: the key has 10 entries for only 7 printed questions.
